decision: The layer of two coding harnesses is named the EXECUTIVE WORKBENCH.
why: The name already existed in the record and was used exactly once. Codex's review of the
original proposal rejected placing the layer 'below the parties' on the grounds that
'calling it an executive risks converting operational capacity into implied authority',
and record/designs/shadow-executive-trial.md settled on 'an executive workbench, not a
government'. Every other document then kept saying 'executive layer', so the corrected
name lived in the argument for it and nowhere else.
'Workbench' names a place where instruments are built and tested and carries no
implication that building them confers standing to use them. The thing has capacity, not
renamed_in: CLAUDE.md (and AGENTS.md, which symlinks it) — the standing instructions both harnesses load

why: Each records what was true when it was written. Editing them to match a name chosen
afterwards would be rewriting the record to agree with the present — the failure this
repository exists to make impossible. Raw material is append-only; a committed
pre-registration IS the instrument that was sent; the ledgers are hash-chained; the
Three balloted clauses read 'The executive cannot adopt anything', 'The executive cannot
interpret its own prohibitions conclusively', and 'The executive takes no unlogged
exception'. Those exact sentences were put to five parties in ratification-01 and are
frozen. A ratification-02 may restate them under the new name, but the change must be
visible as a change to the balloted text, not applied silently to what was already asked.

not_renamed_in_quotations: Lines quoting Codex, the parties, or the scope statement keep their original wording.
Rewriting a quotation to use a name coined afterwards is fabrication (D-53).
what_this_does_not_change: No authority, no scope, no prohibition, and no capability changes with the name.
The directory record/executive/ keeps its path: renaming it would invalidate paths already
written into the hash-chained action log and the context pins, and a name is not worth
breaking the record's own references for.
